Mina, Vanessa — I pulled the ledger and ran a tentative match against the incoming CSV. Findings:
- The gross payment amount matches our bank credit (EUR 126,432.50) but the invoice-level amounts in remittance_20270522.pdf add up to EUR 124,980.50 — gap of EUR 1,452.00.
- The difference appears to be VAT rounding on three invoices where Clearwater applied VAT at the line level.
- Our provisional policy: apply payment to the oldest open invoices first, then allocate remainder to subsequent invoices. For VAT tagging on EU reports we should: 1) preserve customer-specified VAT allocation when provided, otherwise 2) apply VAT according to invoice tax lines and note rounding adjustments.

I’ve attached a CSV with the bank trace we received from BankNorth (bank_trace_20270522.csv) and a temporary invoice bundle export (invoice_bundle_0427-05.pdf) for reference. If we proceed with provisional apply, we’ll post EUR 124,980.50 and hold EUR 1,452.00 in unapplied suspense pending Marta's confirmation. Alternatively, Marta can send a corrected remittance reflecting the precise VAT splits.

Proposed next step: Mina to ask for per-invoice VAT amounts; if no response in 48h we post per policy and create a suspense ticket.

Karthik
Senior Accountant — Receivables
Redwood Inference
